newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet CFO sees profit in Q3 at earliest.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet CFO sees profit in Q3 at earliest.

text.p: ValuJet Inc's chief financial officer on Thursday said the third quarter of 1997 was the earliest that the discount airline could expect to return to profitability.

"The third quarter represents an opportunity of profitability, and we are working very hard to achieve that," ValuJet CFO Stephen Nevin told analysts at the Robinson-Humphrey Co Inc annual institutional conference in Atlanta.

Nevin said in an interview afterwards that achieving profitability during that period would depend on "everything coming together," including satisfactory passenger revenues. Nevin declined to indicate the size of the profit the airline hoped to achieve.
He said a rise in March load factor to 62.1 percent, from 56 percent in February, was an encouraging sign. "April looks good, but I don't know if we can beat March," Nevin told analysts.
The airline has been operating at a loss since the second quarter of 1996, a period in which one of its passenger flights crashed in the Florida Everglades, killing all 110 people aboard.

Shortly afterward, federal regulators shut down the airline after alleging maintenance difficulties. Since returning to operations, the airline has faced close scrutiny by the Federal Aviation Administration.
The company now operates 24 planes that fly to 172 destinations. Nevin said ValuJet planned to operate "close to 30" aircraft by summmer. "Whether that's June or July, I can't tell you," he said.
